answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond and buys one karst conduit slot: the first costs 25 credits, the kth costs 25+5(k-1), so the 1,000th costs 5,020 and 1,000 fakes pay 2,522,500 plus 80,000 locked. Before work, the identity sends a whisper test pulse through its conduit; an auditor recomputes registry, pulse timing, and nectar flow, rejecting any slot whose pulse or flow mismatches. Sharing a conduit exposes two pulses and burns both bonds; a rented pulse fails because its key does not match the owner. An honest agent pays 25 once and recovers the bond after a clean window.
